claims.text: In a multi-stage Dockerfile each FROM starts a new stage from its own base image; by default the last stage becomes the built image (--target can pick another); COPY --from=<stage> copies files from an earlier stage; nothing else from earlier stages is kept.

DonHang.Api/Dockerfile@stage-1 lines 19-28: FROM mcr.microsoft.com/dotnet/aspnet:10.0 AS final, WORKDIR /app, RUN apt-get ... libgssapi-krb5-2, COPY --from=build /app ., EXPOSE 8080, ENV ASPNETCORE_URLS=http://+:8080, ENTRYPOINT ["dotnet", "DonHang.Api.dll"].
The aspnet image contains the ASP.NET Core and .NET runtimes but no SDK; the SDK image is several times larger (917MB tagged locally vs 241MB for donhang-api:stage-1 on the generator's machine).
claims.source_hint: .NET docs: container images; docker images on the generator's machine

claims.text: EXPOSE records the port the container listens on (documentation, it does not publish it); ENTRYPOINT sets the command a container from the image starts with; ASPNETCORE_URLS sets Kestrel's listening URLs.
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: Dockerfile EXPOSE, ENTRYPOINT; ASP.NET Core docs: ASPNETCORE_URLS

claims.text: In donhang-api:stage-1, dotnet --list-sdks prints nothing, dotnet --list-runtimes lists Microsoft.AspNetCore.App and Microsoft.NETCore.App 10.0.x, /src does not exist and /app holds DonHang.Api.dll among other files; docker images donhang-api shows one image of about 241MB.
claims.source_hint: generator check: docker run --rm --entrypoint sh donhang-api:stage-1 -c ... (runtimes 10.0.12)

claims.text: A runtime-only final image is smaller to store and download and has a smaller attack surface (fewer installed programs to misuse or patch).
claims.source_hint: Docker docs: multi-stage builds / best practices; outline item 3

claims.text: The final COPY --from=build step reruns after a code change because the build stage's published output changed.
The build stage copies only DonHang.Domain/, DonHang.Infrastructure/ and DonHang.Api/ into /src (not tests, app or samples).
